read.skipped: Reference list and appendix generated-program listings (Fig 11-15) skimmed; Tables 7-9 CodeXGLUE not recorded in detail

question: Can unit-test feedback, used in actor-critic RL finetuning and in test-time refine/repair, make pretrained code LMs solve harder program-synthesis problems?
hypothesis: Next-token training ignores unit-test signals; using test outcomes as dense critic-based rewards in training and as feedback at inference improves functional correctness.
contributions: CodeRL actor-critic framework using unit-test returns with greedy baseline and token-level critic values
Critic Sampling inference: refine passing programs from critic-chosen seeds, repair failing ones with error messages
SOTA on APPS and zero-shot MBPP

method.summary: Pretrain CodeT5-770M, warm-start on APPS with cross-entropy, train a small critic to predict unit-test outcome of sampled programs, then finetune the actor with Lce+Lrl. At inference sample N=200 programs, test on example tests, refine passers from critic-selected prefixes and repair the top failing program using error type and message (one round max).
method.task: program synthesis from natural language (APPS, MBPP)

datasets.name: APPS
datasets.preprocessing: same as Hendrycks et al. 2021; avg 23.2 solutions, 21.2 unit tests per problem

datasets.name: MBPP
datasets.preprocessing: prompt: description + 'Your code should satisfy these tests:' + 3 asserts

models.name: CodeT5-large (CodeRL actor)
models.context: source 600 / target 512 on APPS; 768/600 in NTP pretraining

models.name: Critic
models.architecture: CodeT5-small (for CodeT5 actors); GPT2-small (for GPT actors)

training.objective: Lce then Lce+Lrl with equal weights; Lrl REINFORCE with greedy baseline and critic token value (Eq 14), single sample per step; returns -1.0 compile, -0.6 runtime, -0.3 failed test, +1.0 pass
training.lr: pretrain MSP peak 2e-4, NTP peak 1e-4; APPS warm-start 0 to 2e-5 then to 1e-5; MBPP finetune constant 2e-5
training.lr_schedule: linear decay with 1000 warmup steps (pretraining); APPS: warmup 500 steps then polynomial power 0.5 decay
training.batch_size: pretrain MSP 2048 (also text says concatenated to 512), NTP 256; APPS warm-start 64; MBPP 32
training.epochs: MSP: 150 epochs CSN + 10 GCPY; NTP 10; APPS warm-start 10; MBPP 60
training.hardware: 16 A100-40G GPUs on GCP kubernetes (pretraining); 1 A100 for finetuning
training.compute: pretraining about 21 days; APPS warm-start about 30 hours on one A100; MBPP under 30 min
training.wall_clock: MSP 10 days CSN + 5 days GCPY, NTP 6 days

other.critic_training: actor frozen; critic trained on sampled programs plus ground-truth programs labelled PassedTest

inference.decoding: nucleus sampling; beam search in ablations of Tables 2-3
inference.temperature: 1.2 for CodeT5 on MBPP (GPT baseline 0.5); APPS not stated
inference.samples: N=200 per problem in Critic Sampling; k up to 1000; 200 programs for qualitative analysis
inference.prompting: APPS prompt format of Hendrycks; MBPP description + asserts

parameters.M: 1 (top failing programs sent to repair; 2 and 4 tested)
parameters.rounds: at most one repair and/or refine round
parameters.seed_upsampling: N/|P| for refine, N/M for repair

limits: Critic training adds cost beyond the actor, though the authors say a GPT-2-small critic suffices.
Example tests are weaker than hidden tests, giving false positives that cap Critic Sampling gains (Fig 8).
Only one round of refine/repair is used; refine adds little to 1@1000 because n@k pool grows.
CodeRL raises runtime-error rate even while compile errors fall.
Lrl alone suffers vanishing gradients; needs Lce warm start and Lce+Lrl.
Single runs; no seeds or variance reported; many numbers are small (pass@1 2.69%).
Generated code may be biased, insecure; needs human verification.
Results are 2022; the strongest baselines (GPT-J, Codex 12B) have dated.
